{"rule": "Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and a new passage of about 250 words in the text field.", "text": "The boat had been pulled high above the tide line and turned keel-up on the shingle, the way his grandfather had always done it before winter. Tomas walked around it twice before he touched it. The paint had gone chalky along the strakes, and there was a place near the stern where the wood had been patched with something that did not quite match.

His mother waited at the top of the beach with her coat pulled tight. She had said she would not come down, and she had not.

He crouched and ran his palm along the hull. Sound, mostly. He rapped his knuckles at the patch and it answered dull, and he made a note of that without needing to write it anywhere. Underneath, in the shadow of the keel, someone had tucked the oars, wrapped in sacking against the damp. The old man had thought about spring, then. Even in October. Even knowing.

Tomas dragged the oars out and unwrapped them. The leathers were worn through where they met the thole pins, and he turned one over and found his grandfather's mark burned into the loom, the same crooked T he had put on everything he owned.

"Well?" his mother called.

"She'll float."

"That's not what I asked."

He stood and looked at the water, flat and grey and going out. Then he set his shoulder to the gunwale and pushed, and the boat rocked once on the stones before it began, slowly, to turn."}
